summary: Coeur d'Alene National Forest lookout: a 40-foot pole L-4 tower built in 1936 and destroyed in 1960; a 2024 visit found only footings and two benchmarks.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1960. A 2024 visit found the footings and two benchmarks, and the writers saw nothing else.

events.note: A camp was located on the site
Jay Murray, named on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page

evidence.supports: 1930 camp; 1936 40-foot pole L-4 tower; destroyed 1960; 1946 Peacock
evidence.quote: 1930: camp. 1936: 40' pole L-4 tower. Destroyed 1960. Known lookout personnel: 1946: Mr. and Mrs. Clyde Peacock.

evidence.supports: camp located on the site in 1930
Mr. and Mrs. Clyde Peacock named for 1946
footings and two benchmarks found on the visit
evidence.quote: We were quickly able to find the footings for this lookout tower as well as two benchmarks.

evidence.supports: nothing else remains; view gone as trees grew up
evidence.quote: nothing else appears to remain at this site, even the view is gone now that all the surrounding trees have had time to grow well up and around where the tower once sat.
Capitol Hill is an easy drive up
We encountered a fair bit of people on the roads leading up to this spot

corrections.why: The record says unknown. Both sites describe a 40-foot pole L-4 tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Idaho Fire Lookouts page adds Jay Murray for 1937; firelookout.com lists only the Peacocks for 1946. The lists differ in coverage and do not contradict each other.

notes_for_editor: Probably the same lookout as us-id-capitol-hill: same name, same Coeur d'Alene National Forest, and both sites give the same 1936 build and 1960 destruction. The story for us-id-capitol-hill cites the same two pages. Merge decision for a human. Coordinates differ: this record's point (47.52854, -115.94905) is about 3.8 km from firelookout.org's Capitol Hill point (47.55929, -115.97153). Elevation 5,318 ft (about 1,621 m) is from firelookout.com and is not stored as a facts key. Neither source states an access rule; left at unknown.
